WE HAVE HEARD OF MAKING MILK FROM WATER BUT
WHO EVER HEARD OF MAKING HOOPCH FROM MILK.

Year after year milk is made from water, perhaps not so exaggerated but verily milk dealers have diluted it with water but who on this little green earth of ours, has ever heard of any guy using a milk can for hooch. Yea, recently the prohibition agents confiscated this original still. It appears the bootleggers will go to any extreme to make their little "spirits of nitre" for the average human and in the past they have used many pipes and wash boilers etc., but now since being caught they cant fool the Agents any more. Milk may be for babies but first smell the container.

N Y POLICE DEPT OPENS HUGE RADIOPHONE BROADCASTING STATION..TO SEND CUT DESCRIPTIONS OF CRIMINALS AND LISTS OF CASUALTIES,AS WELL AS TO BROADCAST MUSIC AND OTHER ENTERTAINMENT PROGRAMS.

A view in the new "W.L.A.W." radio broadcasting station at New York Police Headquarters. This powerful station, employing a power of 1,600 votes, is equal to any of the largest and most elaborate broadcasting stations in the country. It marks a long step ahead in police work, for the broadcasting of descriptions of criminals and missing persons will literally put millions of Americans on the lookout for the "wanted". In cases where large fires or other fatal disasters occur the names of all casualties will be broadcasted; so that the Police no longer will be flooded by telephone calls from anxious friends and relatives of those involved.
When not in public safety use,the apparatus will be used to broadcast concerts by the splendid police Department band, lectures,and other entertainment programs.

YOUTHFUL ELECTRICAL WIZARD HERE
TO EXPLAIN THEORY AND MANUFACTURE.

Alfred M. Hubbard, aged 21 and his wife, whom he married a month ago, arrived here yesterday and checked in at the Claridge. He brought with him patents on an invention which is said will revolutionize all industry. It generates power from the atmosphere and will make heat and light free. Several tests made, have been reported successful. He arrived in this city to arrange for the manufacture of his dynamo which will weight seventy five pounds when completed. He is waiting for some enterprizing manufacturer to start work on his dynamo, which creates energy without consuming anything tangible.

Dr. Charles P. Steinmetz, world's famous electrical wizard recently caused a great sensation by engineering an electrical storm in his laboratory at Schnectady, N.Y., having all the thrills of a regular storm. Thunder was heard in its heavy velocity and the lightning generator throwing off 120,000 volts caused a mighty flash to strike a tree branch placed in the room for experiments, splitting the wood, as a streak of lightning would do to any harmless tree. Dr. Steinmetz is here shown examining the fragments of tree branch which had been struck by his artificial bolt, the pieces being hurled 25 feet in all directions. A ROMANCE OF TWO POOR STUDENTS.

?r. B. de Platen and Mr. G. Munters, two poor young students have suddenly become famous after years of experimenting at Stockholm University, in inventing a refrigerator which requires no ice. The inventers perfected the original idea, by which heat generates cold. To produce the heat one has to have electric current, gas, oil or waste steam. This invention can be used in any home and eliminates the messy ice-est. By turning on the switch one turns on the heat and produces cold. The patent has been sold in America for £500,000. O.P.S. By pouring water into these small boxes and leaving it for a few minutes, it turns into small blocks of ice. ES

Dr. Coblentz of Wash., D. C. has recently constructed what is probably the most delicate instrument in what is probably the most delicate instrument in distant existence, a tiny motor run by light rays from distant stars - and it took him fifteen years to complete it. The motor also records with unerring accuracy, the heat radiations of celestial bodies hundreds of millions of miles away. A number of astounding facts, hitherto of unknown to science, have been discovered through the use of the delicate apparatus and among the x facts discovered was that heat radiating from a single nebula consisting of 105 stars, were it to be kept steadily shining on sixty drops of water for one hundred years, would only raise it one degree.

TBE B.S.A. JPM GROUPS

The object of this gun is primarily to throw a line at sea where distances are too great to admit the use of a bearing line, from the shore or a lifeboat to a walk. There are however many ways in which it can be applied, as for instance, for throwing a line in the case of fire, in a window or over a building. By some of these guns lines may be directed to any given point with great accuracy, and with certainty even in rough seas. Loading and firing, which are performed very rapidly, need no expert knowledge, and no particular amount of skill. The employer containing the line has merely to be rolled over the barrel where it is held by a catch.

The projectile has then to be slipped into the barrel and the line end protruding from the cylinder attached to the slings on the projectile envelope. After that a cartridge has to be inserted into the chamber and the breach closed to render the gun ready for firing.

RADIO CONCERTS FOR BUS PASSENGERS.

Bus lines in California will soon be serving you radio music with your rides.
The California Transit Company sent the first radio equipped bus out on its regular run to Sacramento, and in spite of the obstacles which confronted the test, the radio concerts for buss passengers was assured.

With only a two step shortwave receiving outfit and handicapped by the necessity of operating with a low antenna, the bus was able to pick up San Francisco and Oakland concerts. There's real entertainment for the bus rider in view.
The chauffer is not forgotten, and he too gets the benefit of the radio concerts.

"CRAB" MACHINE FOR SALVAGING
SUNKEN SHIPS TRIED

A new method of bringing sunken ships to the surface of the coan was tried off Whitestone Landing, L.I., yesterday. Jesse W.Reno, inventor of the es-calator or moving airway, is the inventor of the ship salvaging device. Heretofore it has been impossible to salvage anything which had submerged more than sixty or a hundred feet. The invention of Mr.Reno includes a cylindrical chamber, operated on tractor belts that enable it to clamber about the ocean bottom like a huge crab. The chamber is large enough for two men and contains its own oxygen and air filtering system, which enables the crew to live under water for sixty-four hours. To the "Crab" are fixed two steel drills which bore holes five inches in diameter into the sunken ship. Huge, pantons like inverted water classes are then drawn down by electricity to the tractor and large hooks in them are made fast to the holes in the ship. The pontoons used yesterday had a lifting power of 100 tons. The experiment yesterday was on a sunken submarine chaser which was accidentally sunk last December. Photo shows "Crab" machine.
